title: Hybrid license + credit model for Private/VPC with security questionnaire pilot
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Run a small pilot to validate a hybrid licensing model for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that combines an annual platform license with usage credits and optional managed upgrade windows. Deliverables include pricing matrix, standard contract clauses, an SQA response pack for enterprise security questionnaires, and a playbook for sales to propose migration credits and upgrade cadences.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing matrix with three license SKUs (Core, Plus, Enterprise) and clearly defined credit bundles for token/throughput consumption
Security questionnaire template completed (50 most common enterprise questions) with legal/infosec sign-off
Pilot with 3 enterprise prospects signed to trials with proposed discounts/commitments documented
Sales playbook and datasheet (one-pager) describing upgrade cadence options and support SLAs
Finance model showing unit economics across expected workload mixes and a sensitivity analysis for discounts and overages
decisions: Use hybrid model: Annual base license + prepaid credit bundles for token consumption; offer month-to-month overage billing at a premium
Offer optional 'Managed Upgrade Window' add-on for Enterprise SKU: quarterly non-breaking updates or 18-month LTS with security backports
Three support tiers: Standard (Mon-Fri business hours), Priority (24/7 incident response, 1-hr P0), and Enterprise (dedicated SE + quarterly business reviews)
Discounting: commit-based tier discounts (5% @ 1yr, 12% @ 2yr, negotiable for >$500k ARR), migration credit up to 6 months for customers moving from self-hosted to Redwood Private
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: finalize pricing matrix, legal contract clauses, SQA template; secure infosec & finance sign-off
Week 3-6: run pilot with 3 selected prospects (two from existing PQLs, one channel partner lead); gather willingness-to-pay feedback
Week 7: iterate terms based on pilot; prepare final sales kit and enable GTM
Week 8-12: soft-launch to sales + partners; instrument telemetry for revenue and churn signals
risks: Enterprise buyers expect perpetual on-prem licenses; hybrid model may be perceived as higher TCO unless migration credits are compelling
Discounting complexity could erode margin if sales use inconsistent concessions
Security questionnaire templates may require customer-specific clarifications leading to longer procurement cycles
Operational: implementing prepaid credit metering and overage billing requires billing and telemetry changes (coordination with engineering and finance)
